name: Kaizen
definition: We improve our business operations continuously, always driving for innovation and evolution.

rows.situation: When a small defect shows up in the work
rows.under: Lives with it. Small things are not worth the interruption.
rows.justRight: Fixes it and the condition that produced it, even when the defect looks minor.
rows.over: Stops the whole line for a nick that could have been noted and fixed at the next break.

rows.situation: After a week that already hit the target
rows.under: Leaves the process alone. Good enough is the new standard.
rows.justRight: Asks what still wasted time, and takes one improvement into next week.
rows.over: Restarts the process because it can always be better, and the team never gets a stable week.

rows.situation: When the person doing the work sees a better way
rows.under: They need permission from somewhere that will not look. The idea dies.
rows.justRight: The person who does the work can change it, then tells the people who need to know.
rows.over: Everyone changes the process on their own, and there is no longer a process.

rows.situation: When improvement would delay a deadline
rows.under: Ships the known waste because the date is sacred.
rows.justRight: Takes the improvement that pays back inside the work, and parks the rest.
rows.over: Misses the deadline to polish a process nobody will run this month.

rows.situation: When the standard work is wrong
rows.under: Works around it and never writes the workaround down.
rows.justRight: Updates the standard so the next person does not have to rediscover the fix.
rows.over: Rewrites the standard so often that nobody can tell what the current one is.

rows.situation: When the process needs more than a tweak
rows.under: Tunes a process that should be replaced.
rows.justRight: Improves daily, and still knows when the next step is a different process.
rows.over: Reinvents the operation for the pleasure of it, and the last change never lands.
